Subject: Runtime telemetry and subprocessor custody - initial evidence ask

Hi Michael,

Quick context: Horizon is moving toward a formal procurement review and our technical team needs to validate operational boundaries for any inference provider. Two specific asks we hope you can address with evidence:

1) Runtime telemetry: sample logs or a redacted extract showing what runtime telemetry Redwood collects (request IDs, event types, KV cache metrics, latency traces). We don't need full log dumps — a representative, redacted extract is fine. Please call out which fields are considered PII or customer content and how they're redacted.

2) Subprocessor custody for ephemeral artifacts: in your public docs you reference KV caches and temporary artifacts. We need a mapping of which subprocessors may handle ephemeral runtime data (e.g., cache storage, remote logging, tracing collectors), a short note on retention windows for those artifacts, and whether any of that data ever leaves a customer-dedicated environment.

3) KMS and residency: confirmation of KMS ownership model (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed) for keys that protect telemetry-at-rest, plus a diagram of where telemetry and backups live (regions).

Target timeline: procurement kickoff next week; receiving an evidence bundle by EOD Wednesday 2026-06-02 would be ideal. If you prefer a quick call to walk through the artifacts, we can schedule on Monday afternoon.

Thanks — if you can indicate what you will provide and any limitations that would be great.

Lena Ortiz
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Horizon Health

- Subprocessor custody: we'll include our current subprocessor roster with annotations for runtime-facing roles (logging, tracing, object storage) and retention windows for ephemeral artifacts.
- KMS & residency: we'll attach a diagram showing KMS ownership options (customer-managed via Bring Your Own Key on Dedicated/Private vs Redwood-managed keys for Hosted), and the telemetry storage residency per region.

Lena — attaching the evidence package we discussed. Summary of attachments below and a few clarifications inline.

Attachments included (delivered via secure Drive link):
- redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260530.csv (roster + function column; runtime-facing subprocessors flagged)
- telemetry-extract-sample.json.txt (redacted example; user content removed, timestamps normalized)
- soc2-security-controls-excerpt.pdf (SOC 2 controls relevant to logging/monitoring and subprocessor oversight)
- kms-residency-diagram.png (simple topology showing where telemetry is stored, KMS options, and region boundaries)

Clarifications:
- Telemetry scope: The redacted sample shows our internal event taxonomy (request_received, model_infer_start, model_infer_end, kv_cache_hit/miss, response_sent). Fields that could contain user-generated content are nulled; PII fields are hashed/removed.
- Retention: Default telemetry retention for Hosted is 30 days for fine-grain logs and 365 days for aggregated metrics; for Dedicated & Private customers these defaults can be shortened to meet contract requirements — we can include the change-control steps. Ephemeral KV cache entries are not persisted beyond the inference lifecycle unless caching is explicitly enabled by the customer (and then retention is configurable).
- Subprocessor custody: Runtime-facing subprocessors are primarily (1) our managed logging aggregator provider (collects metrics and sampled traces), (2) a cloud object storage vendor holding telemetry snapshots for a limited retention window, and (3) optional partner integrators when customers enable third-party monitoring. All subprocessors and the functions they perform are in the roster CSV.
- KMS: For Hosted customers, telemetry-at-rest uses Redwood-managed keys by default with HSM-backed keys for root; customers can request BYOK in Dedicated/Private — diagram shows where keys are applied.

Two notes on limitations: (a) we cannot surface raw customer content from logs — all extracts are redacted and sampled; (b) if Horizon needs an on-prem escrow of telemetry datasets, we'll need to scope that as an add-on.

If anything else is required for procurement (e.g., notarized SOC 2 report, SIG questionnaire answers), say the word and we'll queue for the compliance team.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security Programs, Redwood Inference
